solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Stick on the side of the women

definitions.meaning: the staff that holds unspun wool or flax in hand-spinning

definitions.text: on the side of the women
definitions.meaning: the maternal line of a family is called its ... side, so the word serves as an adjective for female kin

explanation.surface: Someone sticks with the women in a dispute, taking their side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick on' reads as a phrasal verb, but 'Stick' is a definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinning staff was traditionally women's work, hence the second, kinship sense of female.

clue.text: Pronouncement not bright about trade union being restricted

indicators.note: the pieces before these words are hemmed in by the word for not bright

parts.note: someone not bright is dim
C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A dim official's statement about a union being curbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reads as concerning, but here it is circa, a crossword staple for C; 'being restricted' says that piece and the union are held within 'not bright'.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal authoritative statement or saying is a synonym of pronouncement.

clue.text: Broken bits the woman's taken across the road

indicators.note: the word for the woman's is stretched across the road abbreviation, enclosing it

parts.note: the woman's, as in the woman is, gives SHE'S
RD is the usual abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: A woman carries some broken pieces over the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Shards of pottery found at a dig are also spelt this way, meaning broken fragments.

clue.text: Scare with amputation being tricky? Much fuss about nothing!

indicators.note: tricky letters are hard to handle, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone frightened by the thought of an awkward amputation is told it is a fuss over nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: SCARE and AMPUTATION together have exactly the fifteen letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for great agitation over a trivial matter, a tempest in a teapot to Americans.

clue.text: Onwards from river

definitions.meaning: as in go ..., meaning forward or onward
the Scottish river flowing into the Firth of ... past Edinburgh

explanation.surface: Moving on from a river crossing.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb meaning forward and the name of a major Scottish river share one spelling.

clue.text: Join a group of abstainers attending a church

parts.note: TT stands for teetotal, people abstaining from alcohol

explanation.surface: An invitation to join the temperance society that meets at a church.
explanation.definitionFit: To fasten or connect one thing to another is to join them.

clue.text: Fellow with a heavenly body looked up to

definitions.text: Fellow with a heavenly body looked up to

parts.words: Fellow with a heavenly body looked up to
parts.note: sounds like an admired hunk, but it is the face people see on the lunar disc, literally looked up at in the sky

explanation.surface: A handsome man everyone admires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heavenly body' suggests good looks and 'looked up to' esteem; both are literal here, a celestial body seen overhead.
explanation.definitionFit: The fanciful figure of a face imagined in the markings of the lunar surface.

clue.text: Came down and hit glade, crashing

indicators.note: crashing smashes the letters of the two words into a new order

explanation.surface: Something descended and smashed into a forest clearing.
explanation.definitionFit: To get off a vehicle or settle after flight is to come down or land.

clue.text: Having many American stories?

parts.note: stories is the American spelling of storeys, the floors of a building, not tales

explanation.surface: Someone with a fund of tales from the USA.
explanation.walkthrough: In American English a building's floors are stories, so many stories means a tall building.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes a tower block with a large number of floors.

clue.text: Son with inferior status on account of lack of intelligence?

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
being low in rank is lowness

explanation.surface: A son held back because of his supposed lack of brains.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'slow' as dull-witted is a slightly loose sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Being slow on the uptake is being dull-witted, a want of quick intelligence.

clue.text: Cold minister, not cold when conveying a description of God

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

indicators.note: the shortened clergyman carries the letter A inside him
not tells us to drop the letter for cold from the clergyman

parts.note: a rector is a parish clergyman
C again for cold, this time the letter removed

explanation.surface: A chilly clergyman offering a description of God.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not cold' takes the C out of RECTOR to leave RETOR; 'when conveying' puts A inside, REATOR, after the opening C.
explanation.definitionFit: God is called the Maker of all things, the one who brought the world into being.

clue.text: Clique hiding behind shelter lusting after woman?

indicators.note: the clique word comes after the shelter word in the answer

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind
a ring is a closed group of people, a clique

explanation.surface: A gang skulks behind cover, eyeing a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogling with a sly, lecherous look is a sign of lust.

clue.text: Air passengers making descent may soon become so poorly

definitions.text: Air passengers making descent may soon become so
definitions.meaning: a landing plane drops below the clouds, so its passengers end up literally beneath the skies' conditions

explanation.surface: Fliers coming in to land may start feeling sick.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is literal: descending through cloud puts people below the weather.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means feeling unwell or out of sorts.

clue.text: Colour of Oxon town reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means we hear the town's name spoken

parts.note: Bicester is a town in Oxfordshire, abbreviated Oxon, pronounced 'bister'

explanation.surface: Asking what colour an Oxfordshire town is said to be.
explanation.walkthrough: Bicester, a market town in Oxfordshire, is pronounced 'bister', which matches the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A brownish pigment made from soot, used for ink wash drawings.

clue.text: Beginners perhaps fall down in river

indicators.note: the falling water sits inside the river

parts.note: the Tees is a river in north-east England
rain is what falls down from clouds

explanation.surface: Novices might tumble into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fall down' looks like a stumble but means precipitation.
explanation.definitionFit: People learning a trade are novices, one example of beginners.

clue.text: Italian script containing English snippets of news?

parts.note: MS is short for manuscript, a written script

explanation.surface: An Italian text with English bits of news inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Short pieces in a newspaper or bulletin are called news pieces or reports.

clue.text: Dad's role is diverting elderly females perhaps

indicators.note: diverting turns the letters aside into a new order

explanation.surface: Dad's part is entertaining the grannies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diverting' looks like amusing; it signals the anagram of DADSROLE.
explanation.definitionFit: An affectionate British term for old women, often grandmotherly types.

clue.text: This person crossing street to block entrance — a downcast soul?

indicators.note: the combined pieces sit in the doorway, blocking it

parts.note: a door is an entrance

indicators.note: the setter's pronoun straddles the street abbreviation

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: Someone crosses the road to stand miserably in a doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A gloomy prophet of disaster is a pessimist, a soul given to despondency.

clue.text: What's found in bathroom or toilet? Nothing!

parts.note: loo is British slang for toilet
FA, short for sweet Fanny Adams, is British slang for nothing at all

explanation.surface: A question about bathroom contents, answered with nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweet FA (Fanny Adams) is a British euphemism for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A dried gourd sponge used for scrubbing in the bath or shower.

clue.text: Mathematical assumption gives answer at end of sequence

parts.note: Z ends the alphabetical sequence

explanation.surface: A maths hypothesis yields the answer at the close of a series.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of sequence' is not the last letter of 'sequence' but the end of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A German-derived term for an educated guess about the form of a solution, later verified.

clue.text: Exile's home set up in British wood

indicators.note: the turned word sits inside the tree

parts.note: ash is a timber tree

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the word is read upwards

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: An exile's house built in a British forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'home' means at home, i.e. in; 'set up' turns that word upwards in this down clue, and 'in' places it inside the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: To expel someone from their country is to send them into exile.

clue.text: Book presenting two sides, full of incisiveness

indicators.note: the two side letters are filled with the sharpness word

parts.note: L and R, left and right
sharpness or bite, as in an edge to a remark

explanation.surface: A book giving both sides of an argument with sharp insight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two sides' also hints at a ledger's debit and credit columns.
explanation.definitionFit: An account book in which a business records transactions.

clue.text: Theatrical female shows a mad need, getting worse always with time

indicators.note: worse letters are deteriorating into a jumble

parts.note: ever means always, as in for ever
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: An actress whose wild cravings worsen year after year.
explanation.walkthrough: Barry Humphries' stage character, the Australian housewife superstar.
explanation.definitionFit: A comic drag persona played by Barry Humphries, a famous female character of stage and TV.

clue.text: Anxious attitude a German shows

indicators.note: the letters are on show within the words attitude a German

explanation.surface: A German displays a nervous attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs from the end of 'attitude' into 'German'.
explanation.definitionFit: Anxious to do something means keen or impatient to do it.

clue.text: Possibly a small bit without soft edge

indicators.note: without means the soft letter is dropped
edge places that dropped letter at the front of the word

parts.note: a particle is a tiny piece
P is piano, the musical marking for soft

explanation.surface: Perhaps a tiny fragment without a smooth rim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly a' is the definition: the word 'a' is an example of the part of speech.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar 'a' is the indefinite member of this word class, alongside 'the'.

clue.text: Good, like noisy cattle looking healthy?

parts.note: lowing is the mooing of cattle

explanation.surface: Cattle that sound well are evidently in fine health.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosy, radiant complexion signals good health.

clue.text: Fasteners securing carriage aboard ship

indicators.note: the carriage is placed inside the ship letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
a trap is a light horse-drawn carriage

explanation.surface: Fixings holding a carriage in place on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Bands of leather or webbing with buckles hold things fast.

clue.text: Farmer managed to get hitched to songstress

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business
Cher is a famous American singer

explanation.surface: A man managed to marry a pop singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who owns or works a cattle ranch is a kind of farmer.
